I completely disagree. Why else is so much thought and consideration given to how to facilitate fair and honest discussion. Upvotes, downvotes, bans, etc.

Call it what you will but this sites like this begin and end on the discussions brought about by the media aggregated.

There's no reason why /v/fairandhonestdiscussion can't exist alongside /v/cutestcatIsawoutsidetoday (both subs available, FTR)

The whole point of splitting content into user-created subs is so that many types of content can exist on the same network. Rather than banning certain types of content you don't want to see on the site, why not propose features or systems that would let you easily source content you enjoy? Like starting a meta-sub to share subs that focus on deep discussions, or introducing something like the multireddit feature.

I wouldn't subscribe to a sub like aww either, but I disagree with the content being "garbage". Sometimes looking at a cute photo can be just what someone needs to lift their mood. Their is nothing wrong with having such sites on Voat.

Memes can be a problem when they start displacing serious discussion within a sub. When this occurs, it is due to bad moderation; moderators surrendering to populism. The solution is for moderators to set rules on what kind of content is and is not on topic. When moderators delete this content when it is submitted, it doesn't overtake the sub.
